resources.title: What is Bonsai? (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It comes from the biggest bonsai teaching site, and it shows that the 'tiny tree' is made by pruning, potting and patience, not by its seed.

resources.title: What Makes Bonsai So Mysterious? (History of Simple Things)
resources.why: It tells the history of how a Chinese and Japanese art of potted trees became a worldwide obsession, which shows bonsai as an art form and not a plant product.

resources.title: Why Are Bonsai Trees So Small?
resources.why: It says plainly that bonsai are 'ordinary trees and shrubs, not hereditary dwarfs', and that the same tree in open ground could grow 15 to 30 m tall.

resources.title: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map (interactive)
resources.why: Type in your ZIP code to find your own climate zone, which is the first fact you need before choosing a tree that can live outside where you are.

resources.title: Indoor Bonsai 'All You Need To Know' (Herons Bonsai)
resources.why: Peter Chan, a nurseryman with decades of experience, sorts the few species that cope indoors from the many that don't, and shows you round his own indoor collection.

resources.title: What actually kills an outdoor tree when it is kept indoors? (Bonsai Mirai forum)
resources.why: Practitioners explain the slow death step by step: indoor light is too dim for photosynthesis, the tree misses its dormancy, and it uses up its reserves until it fails, often by the third season.

resources.title: Indoor Bonsai (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: It explains plainly that every bonsai is an outdoor tree, and that a temperate tree denied its winter dormancy can grow itself to death.

resources.title: Indoor Light Reality: Why Plants Need More Light Than You Think
resources.why: Its lux figures are a shock: a bright windowsill gives a small fraction of outdoor sun, and the light falls off sharply only a metre or two back into the room.

resources.title: Bonsai Design Principles for Beginners (Bonsai Heirloom)
resources.why: It walks through the guidelines that make a tree look old and convincing, which gives you a checklist to use on any bonsai you see.

resources.title: How to create a Nebari (surface roots) by Michael Hagedorn (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: A well-known American bonsai artist shows why a strong spread of surface roots is the first thing an experienced eye looks at, and how one is built.

resources.title: How to create a good Bonsai trunk (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Once you know about taper and reverse taper, you will start spotting trunks that look like telephone poles everywhere.

resources.title: Bonsai pots (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It opens with the line 'a tree is a tree, and a pot is only a pot' and shows how pot shape and colour can echo the bark, leaves or flowers.

resources.title: Bonsai Tools - All You Need To Know (Herons Bonsai)
resources.why: A veteran nurseryman sorts the tools you really need from the expensive extras that beginners buy too early.

resources.title: Bonsai Tools Basics: Concave Branch Cutter VS Knob Cutter (Wazakura Japan)
resources.why: A side-by-side demonstration makes clear why one cutter leaves a flat hollow and the other a deep scoop, and when each wound heals better.

resources.title: Tips for using basic bonsai tools (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: A working professional gives small, specific tips you won't find in a catalogue, such as cutting thick wire in the notch and not at the tips, and using the blunt end of the concave cutter for big branches.

resources.title: Garden Myth Busters: Using Bleach to Disinfect Tools
resources.why: It tests the standard advice to dip tools in bleach and finds it rusts your expensive steel, which makes cleaning your tools a question of evidence and not habit.

resources.title: How Trees Bend the Laws of Physics (Veritasium)
resources.why: A suction pump can't lift water more than about 10 m, yet trees lift it over 100 m, and Veritasium shows how negative pressure makes that possible.

resources.title: Transpiration and water transport in trees: the cohesion-tension theory
resources.why: A focused walk-through that follows the chain from stomata to xylem to roots, which is the lesson's main sequence.

resources.title: Cohesion-Tension Theory (LibreTexts General Botany)
resources.why: A free, open textbook page you can come back to whenever you need to know why a tree in a dry bonsai pot wilts within hours.

resources.title: Passive water ascent in a tall, scalable synthetic tree
resources.why: Engineers built an artificial tree that lifts water with no pump at all, which is striking proof that the physics in the videos really works.

resources.title: Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration: Crash Course Botany #5
resources.why: Crash Course presents photosynthesis and respiration as income and spending, which is the energy-budget idea this lesson is built on.

resources.title: Distinguishing vigorous growth from healthy growth (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: Side-by-side photos teach you to read shoot length, leaf size and bud size to judge whether a tree has the energy for wiring or heavy pruning.

resources.title: How much to prune?
resources.why: It explains why the arborists' rule of 'no more than 25 to 30 percent a year' exists: every cut removes stored carbohydrate as well as future leaf area.

resources.title: Bonsai techniques: Backbudding in Bonsai by Heike van Gunst
resources.why: You watch a bonsai professional make a tree grow new buds on old wood, which shows that the tree's vigour can be moved around on purpose.

resources.title: Bonsai techniques: Backbudding on Pine Bonsai by Koji Hiramatsu
resources.why: Pines are known for refusing to back-bud, so seeing a Japanese professional get around that shows how stubborn apical dominance can be.

resources.title: Maintenance Pruning part two: Pinching Out Deciduous Trees (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: Its diagrams circle the exact buds that wake up once you pinch the tip, so the auxin idea becomes something you can do with your fingers.

resources.title: A Growing Stem Inhibits Bud Outgrowth – The Overlooked Theory of Apical Dominance
resources.why: This open-access paper questions the simple textbook story that 'auxin from the tip suppresses buds', so you see that the science is still being argued.

resources.title: How Trees Bend the Laws of Physics (Veritasium)
resources.why: Trees pull water up through very strong negative pressure, and once you see how fragile that water column is, a wilting tree makes sense.

resources.title: Distinguishing vigorous growth from healthy growth (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: It explains why a tree with good colour can still be too weak to work on, which is the energy-budget idea seen from the bench.

resources.title: Pruning Myths (Linda Chalker-Scott handout)
resources.why: A university horticulturist looks at popular pruning beliefs one by one, which is a good way to test the idea that cutting a tree back makes it stronger right away.

resources.title: The secret language of trees – Camille Defrenne and Suzanne Simard (TED-Ed)
resources.why: A short animation of the fungal network that trades sugar for nutrients under every healthy tree, presented by the researcher behind the 'wood wide web' idea.

resources.title: Radish germination timelapse (root hair close-up)
resources.why: Root hairs are usually invisible, and this time-lapse shows how fast a fuzz of them appears behind the root tip.

resources.title: Why Does Over-Watering Kill Plants? (ScienceABC)
resources.why: Oxygen moves through water about 10,000 times more slowly than through air, which explains how a soaked tree can drown and die of thirst.

resources.title: All About Akadama (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: It shows why bonsai growers pay for gritty baked clay instead of potting soil: the air gaps are the point.

resources.title: How Trees Compartmentalize Decay (CODIT Explained Using a Large Oak)
resources.why: On a real oak, an arborist shows that the tree walls off rot instead of repairing it, and the short makes that point on its own.

resources.title: Woods Whys: How Do Trees Heal Wounds on Trunks and Branches? (Northern Woodlands)
resources.why: A clear, short read on the 'seal, don't heal' idea: a chemical reaction zone first, then wound wood that grows over the damage.

resources.title: A Pictorial Primer for Proper Pruning (Alex Shigo)
resources.why: Drawings by the man who named the branch collar show exactly where to cut and why a flush cut opens the tree to decay.

resources.title: Pruning Sealants (University of Arizona Extension)
resources.why: An extension publication on whether you should paint a cut, a debate that bonsai forums still argue about.

resources.title: Bonsai and Winter Dormancy: Dormancy is not optional
resources.why: The title makes the point: keeping a temperate bonsai warm indoors to protect it slowly kills it.

resources.title: Understanding Dormancy and Chilling (University of Minnesota Extension)
resources.why: Trees keep count of cold hours before they will wake, which protects them from a false spring.

resources.title: Winter care for Bonsai (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It sorts trees into tropical, deciduous and conifer, and warns that roots in a pot face cold from every side, including underneath.

resources.title: Fact Sheet FS528 (Rutgers Cooperative Extension)
resources.why: An extension fact sheet on keeping container plants alive through winter, where root hardiness is the weak point.

resources.title: CODIT & MICROS by Dr. Alex Shigo
resources.why: Alex Shigo, the scientist who proved that trees don't heal like skin, explains it himself, which makes this a primary source for the misconception revisit.

resources.title: Wound Dressings: Results of Studies Over 13 Years (Shigo & Shortle, 1983)
resources.why: 275 wounded trees were cut open over 13 years and no dressing stopped decay; the individual tree mattered more than any product.

resources.title: Winter Care for Bonsai (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: It names wind, not cold, as the biggest winter danger, which is a good test of whether you can tie hardiness back to water loss.

resources.title: Why Is My Bonsai Tree Dying? Here's How to Bring It Back to Life (Bonsai Direct)
resources.why: Work from symptoms back to causes such as soggy soil starving roots of oxygen, and check whether you can predict the problem before reading the answer.

resources.title: Perched Water Table: don't add rocks to your plant pots
resources.why: It shows why a layer of gravel at the bottom of a pot makes waterlogging worse, which most people find hard to believe until they see it.

resources.title: BONSAI SOIL vs POTTING MIX: Does it make a difference?
resources.why: It tests the idea that ordinary potting soil is fine for bonsai by growing trees in both, so you can see the answer instead of just being told.

resources.title: An Introduction to Bonsai Soils (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: It turns 'use a gritty mix' into exact particle sizes (2–3 mm, 4–5 mm, 6–7 mm for pines) and explains why sieving out the dust matters as much as the material you choose.

resources.title: Bonsai substrate, Bjorn Bjorholm
resources.why: Bjorholm spent six years as an apprentice in Japan, and here he explains in plain terms why each part of the mix is there.

resources.title: To Akadama, or not to Akadama? (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It looks honestly at whether the expensive Japanese clay is worth it, given that it breaks down within about two years.

resources.title: Bonsai soil, recommended substrate mixtures (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It gives the role of each ingredient and ready mixes for different kinds of tree, like 50/25/25 for deciduous trees and equal thirds for pines.

resources.title: Why we don't use Akadama
resources.why: A grower makes the case against the 'standard' ingredient, which pushes you to think about what each component actually does.

resources.title: Watering Bonsai trees (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: A short lesson from one of the best-known bonsai teaching channels that shows how to read the tree and the soil instead of following the calendar.

resources.title: How To Water Your Bonsai In The Summer
resources.why: Summer heat is when watering on a fixed schedule kills trees, and this shows how much a tree's needs change with the weather.

resources.title: Watering Bonsai; how to water your trees (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: It lists everything that changes how fast a pot dries (sun, wind, pot size, soil, season), so 'every Tuesday' falls apart.

resources.title: Understanding Bonsai Fertilizer (N, P, K, Mg, Ca, Fe, S)
resources.why: It covers the nutrients beyond the three numbers on the bag, including the magnesium and iron that keep leaves green.

resources.title: The secret of bonsai fertilisation, the power of NPK (Mistral Bonsai)
resources.why: It is written by a working bonsai nursery and connects each nutrient to something you can see on the tree, ending with how to fix iron chlorosis.

resources.title: Soil Basics Part II: Chemical Properties of Soil (UMass Extension)
resources.why: A clear university explainer of cation-exchange capacity and pH that shows why a soil can hold nutrients or let them wash away.

resources.title: Iron Chlorosis: Symptoms, Causes and Solutions (Utah State Extension)
resources.why: It explains the puzzle that yellow leaves often grow in soil full of iron, because high pH locks the iron away from the roots.

resources.title: Bonsai Repotting Made Easy (Herons Bonsai)
resources.why: Peter Chan, who founded Britain's best-known bonsai nursery, makes a job most beginners dread look simple.

resources.title: Repotting theory and Bonsai substrate explained (Bjorn Bjorholm)
resources.why: It explains why you repot, including how soil breaks down over time, so timing and root pruning stop feeling like arbitrary rules.

resources.title: Repotting a Trident Maple: Securing the Tree in the Pot (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: Step-by-step photos of the wiring that keeps a tree from rocking in its pot and tearing the new roots.

resources.title: Repotting and Root-Pruning Bonsai, Part 1 (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: It explains how much root you can safely cut and why the season, judged by bud swell, decides how well the tree recovers.

resources.title: Where to place your Bonsai tree (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Its warning that light drops sharply just a few feet from a window explains why so many indoor trees slowly die.

resources.title: Growing Bonsai Indoors Under LED Light
resources.why: It shows a real indoor setup that works, which makes 'can grow lights replace the sun?' concrete.

resources.title: Important Considerations for Providing Supplemental Light to Indoor Plants (Iowa State Extension)
resources.why: University guidance that replaces lux and watts with the measures plants actually respond to, so you can compare grow lights on the right numbers.

resources.title: Lighting Plants Indoors (Michigan State University Floriculture)
resources.why: Written by plant-lighting researchers, it explains PPFD and how much light a plant gets over a day, so you can tell how far a windowsill is from full sun.

resources.title: Overwintering Bonsai trees (Bonsai Empire, with Ryan Neil)
resources.why: Ryan Neil goes through it one temperature band at a time, so you can tell exactly when your own tree needs more than a sheltered bench.

resources.title: Winter Protection of Bonsai (What to when it gets cold) – Growing Bonsai by Jelle
resources.why: A hobbyist shows his own low-cost setup as the frost arrives, which proves you don't need a greenhouse to keep trees alive.

resources.title: How do I overwinter my bonsai plant? – Missouri Botanical Garden
resources.why: A botanical garden's horticulturists put cold frames, unheated garages and heeling in side by side on one short page, so you can choose what fits your space.

resources.title: Winter Care For Bonsai – Bonsai4me
resources.why: It explains why a 'hardy' tree can still die in a pot: its whole root system sits above ground, where it freezes much faster than roots in the soil.

resources.title: Why Your Bonsai Is Dying (And How to Save It) – The Bonsai Barn
resources.why: A fast tour of the usual killers that works as a warm-up before you try the five cases.

resources.title: How to tell when something is wrong with your bonsai – Bonsai Tonight
resources.why: Jonas Dupuich teaches a diagnostic habit: first decide if the problem sits on the leaf surface or comes from inside the tree, which is half of the gate task.

resources.title: What is Iron Chlorosis and What Causes it? – Utah State University Extension
resources.why: It shows why a tree can starve for iron in soil full of iron: above about pH 7 the iron stays locked in the soil.

resources.title: Indoor Bonsai – Bonsai Empire
resources.why: It shows how much weaker window light is than outdoor light, which explains why indoor trees decline slowly instead of dying all at once.

resources.title: How to Prune a Bonsai tree – Bonsai Empire
resources.why: A short, clear demo that separates the regular trim that keeps a tree's shape from the big cuts that build its structure.

resources.title: Natural-target-pruning (ala Alex Shigo) vs close-cut Pruning on pine sapling – Bob Seymour
resources.why: A side-by-side experiment lets you see whether leaving the branch collar really changes how a wound closes.

resources.title: Compartmentalization of decay in trees (CODIT)
resources.why: Shigo found that trees don't heal wounds, they wall them off, and that changed where everyone makes their cuts.

resources.title: Timing cutback to support development goals – Bonsai Tonight
resources.why: The same cut can thicken a trunk or refine a branch depending on the season, and this article shows how to time it to the result you want.

resources.title: Pinching to Manage Bonsai Growth – Bonsai Mirai
resources.why: Ryan Neil presents pinching as a way to manage the tree's energy, not just a trim, which links straight back to physiology.

resources.title: Defoliate Bonsai – When to do it and WHY (Trident Maple example) – bonsai worx
resources.why: The 'why' and 'when' come first, so you learn which trees should never be defoliated before anyone picks up scissors.

resources.title: Leaf pruning vs partial defoliation – Bonsai Tonight
resources.why: Two techniques that look almost the same get very different responses from the tree, and the photos make the difference clear.

resources.title: Focus on defoliation: determining how many leaves to remove – Bonsai Tonight
resources.why: It answers the real question, which is how many leaves to take off and from which parts of the tree, rather than whether to defoliate at all.

resources.title: Bonsai Wiring Made Easy: 1-Branch & 2-Branch Techniques – To Be A Bonsai
resources.why: It shows the anchoring trick that makes wire hold: one wire spans two branches so each anchors the other.

resources.title: You're Removing Your Bonsai Wire At The Wrong Time – Jason Hanrahan, The Bonsai Garden
resources.why: Wire left on a few weeks too long leaves scars that last for years, and this shows how to spot the moment before that happens.

resources.title: Wiring Bonsai trees to shape and bend the branches – Bonsai Empire
resources.why: A clear reference for choosing aluminium or copper wire, picking the gauge and checking the wrapping angle.

resources.title: Bonsai wire – AusBonsai wiki
resources.why: It explains why copper must be annealed and why coils wrapped steeper than about 60° lose their hold, so the 45° rule makes sense.

resources.title: Pruning A Bonsai Recovering From Stress – Gro Bonsai
resources.why: An honest case study of a tree that was pushed too hard, and the year of waiting it needed before more work.

resources.title: Distinguishing vigorous growth from healthy growth in bonsai – Bonsai Tonight
resources.why: It shows that 'healthy' and 'strong enough for heavy work' are not the same, which is the key to judging this year's budget.

resources.title: One Infraction Per Season? – Bonsai Nut forum
resources.why: Experienced growers debate when the 'one major stress per year' rule can bend, and you can watch the 'more work means faster bonsai' idea fall apart.

resources.title: Thicken the trunk of your Bonsai (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: A quick visual case for why a tree has to grow freely, with no pot and no pruning, before its trunk gets any thicker.

resources.title: Create Trunk Taper and Movement with Trunk Chops | Beech Hedgerow Plant to Bonsai (Growing Bonsai by Jelle)
resources.why: Watch a cheap hedge plant turn into a tapered bonsai trunk through repeated rounds of chopping and regrowing.

resources.title: Bonsai Development Series #16: Developing the Trunk with Multiple Sacrifice Branches (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: A black pine with six sacrifice branches, one of them over five feet long after 6–7 years, shows how many years of growth go into a few inches of trunk.

resources.title: Developing Informal Upright Trunks for Deciduous Bonsai (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: Explains the Japanese growing-field method and the catch that surprises most people: after a chop, the base barely thickens until the new section above it catches up.

resources.title: Preserving Jins & Sharis (Herons Bonsai)
resources.why: A veteran UK nurseryman shows how grey, fragile deadwood turns bone-white and lasting with a brush of lime sulfur.

resources.title: Deadwood on Bonsai (Jin, Shari and Uro) (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Its rule to 'follow the live vein upwards from the base' explains how a tree that is mostly dead wood can still be alive.

resources.title: Bristlecone Pines (Illinois State Museum)
resources.why: The wild version of shari: a pine over 4,000 years old kept alive by a single strip of living bark about ten inches wide, which shows why dense, resinous deadwood barely rots.

resources.title: Lime sulfur (Wikipedia)
resources.why: The chemistry behind the rotten-egg smell, and why mixing it with acid can release toxic hydrogen sulfide, so the gloves and goggles stop being optional.

resources.title: How to use Thread Grafting to improve your Bonsai (Mă-Kè Bonsai)
resources.why: Drilling a hole through your own tree's trunk and threading one of its branches through looks crazy, and it is one of the most reliable grafts there is.

resources.title: How to Air Layer (Bonsai Propagation Tutorial) (The Bonsai Supply)
resources.why: Grow roots exactly where you want them while the branch is still on the tree, then cut off a new tree that is already years ahead of a cutting.

resources.title: Grafting Bonsai trees (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Scion, approach and thread grafts side by side, plus a timing twist: two are done in late winter, but approach grafting waits for summer.

resources.title: Layering techniques for Bonsai (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: Shows how one well-placed layer can fix a bad root flare or shorten a trunk that is too tall, which turns propagation into a design tool.

resources.title: From twig to Masterpiece: The 4 Stages of Growing a Bonsai! (Growing Bonsai by Jelle)
resources.why: Helps you see which stage your tree is in, which decides what this year's plan should be.

resources.title: When and how to prune bonsai? (Bonsai Fundamentals) (Growing Bonsai by Jelle)
resources.why: The same cut helps or hurts depending on the month, and this shows how to match pruning to the tree's yearly cycle.

resources.title: Bonsai maintenance calendar (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: A ready-made frame for your 12-month plan: six phases of the tree's year, each with the jobs that cost it the least stress.

resources.title: Chinese Elm Bonsai care (Ulmus) (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Shows why this tree forgives so much: it buds back readily, takes hard pruning, and recovers from beginner mistakes.

resources.title: Making a Classic Broom-Style Chinese Zelkova Bonsai (Bonsai Heirloom)
resources.why: Watch the broom form come together, a fan of fine twigs that only a species with zelkova's eager budding can produce.

resources.title: Zelkova serrata, approx. 120 years, hōki-zukuri (Omiya Bonsai Art Museum)
resources.why: A 120-year-old museum broom zelkova shows where decades of pinching and twig building end up.

resources.title: Chinese elm bonsai winter care (University of Maryland Extension, Ask Extension)
resources.why: A real panic over a tree left out in the cold, answered by an extension expert: the tree is hardy, but roots in a pot are not, which is the key fact for winter care.

resources.title: Expert Juniper Bonsai Pruning: Avoid Subtle Mistakes that Sabotage Your Tree (Growing Bonsai by Jelle)
resources.why: Small habits, like where you cut and how much you take, decide whether a juniper gets denser or quietly weakens.

resources.title: Junipers: Don't Pinch Too Much! (Bonsai Bark, quoting Michael Hagedorn)
resources.why: A professional says it plainly: 'We pinch far too much on junipers.' Use scissors on long shoots a couple of times a year instead.

resources.title: Pinch! Don't Pinch! (Bonsai Bark)
resources.why: Sets Hagedorn's claim that over-pinching 'has been killing junipers for decades' against Kunio Kobayashi's guidance on controlled pinching, so you can judge the misconception yourself.

resources.title: Reversion to Juvenile foliage - Juniper (Bonsai Mirai forum)
resources.why: Real growers figure out why a stressed juniper suddenly sprouts spiky needle foliage, which reads like a health warning the tree is giving you.

resources.title: Partial Defoliation of Japanese Maple Bonsai
resources.why: You see a dense maple canopy thinned leaf by leaf, and you learn why removing the strong outer leaves keeps the weak inner twigs alive.

resources.title: Partial defoliation on shohin Japanese maple (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: Jonas Dupuich shows the technique on a tiny tree with before-and-after photos, so you can see how each cut leads to finer twigs.

resources.title: Winter Care For Bonsai (Bonsai4me)
resources.why: A maple that is fine with frost on its branches can still lose its roots in a frozen pot, and this explains why and how to protect them.

resources.title: Acer palmatum care guide (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: A short reference that ties small leaves to low-nitrogen feeding and says when to protect the tree in a cold frame (below -10 °C).

resources.title: Bonsai techniques: When to repot Bonsai by Ryan Neil
resources.why: Ryan Neil explains timing through what the tree is doing at each stage, not dates on a calendar, and that approach works for any species.

resources.title: Juniper Winter Care. Don't bring it indoors! (Bonsai For Beginners 2)
resources.why: Shows why a conifer's winter needs are very different from a maple's, and why bringing it indoors to be kind can kill it.

resources.title: Seasonal Indicator-based Task List (Bonsai Nut forum)
resources.why: Experienced growers swap calendar dates for signals like bud swell, hardened leaves and leaf drop, which is the shift in thinking this lesson is about.

resources.title: Decandling cork bark black pine bonsai (Why, how and when)
resources.why: Watching someone cut off all the new spring growth on purpose makes sense once you hear that it brings back two shorter-needled shoots in summer.

resources.title: Japanese White Pine Spring Candle Breaking
resources.why: The contrast with black pine: on a single-flush white pine you only break candles part way, because the tree can't regrow what you remove.

resources.title: Which pine species can I decandle? (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: A clear sorting of species into 'decandle' and 'don't', which is the question this lesson asks.

resources.title: Why we decandle pine bonsai (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: Explains the reasons behind decandling (shorter needles, shorter internodes, more branching, balanced energy) and traces the method back to Saichi Suzuki at Daiju-en.

resources.title: Grow Lamp Vs Sunny Windowsill (Ficus benjamina)
resources.why: A side-by-side test of the windowsill myth: same species, two light sources, and you can see the difference.

resources.title: Bonsai techniques: Ficus Bonsai care tips (indoor bonsai) by Peter Chan
resources.why: Peter Chan of Herons Bonsai, one of the best-known UK growers, gives practical advice on keeping ficus healthy indoors.

resources.title: Care guide for the Ficus Bonsai tree (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Gives the actual temperature numbers (above 10 °C minimum, outdoors in summer above 15 °C) that make 'can it live on my sill?' a question you can answer.

resources.title: From 'Mallsai' to Bonsai (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Follows a cheap shop ficus as it is turned into a real bonsai, so the low-light gift-shop tree becomes a project with a future.

resources.title: Prune Now or Lose Next Year's Azalea Bonsai Flowers
resources.why: The title is the lesson: prune a few weeks too late and you cut off next spring's flowers.

resources.title: Post-bloom thinning Satsuki azalea (Bonsai Tonight)
resources.why: Shows how to cut the whorl of shoots behind each spent flower down to a Y, the step that builds the next year's flowering structure.

resources.title: Care guide for the Azalea Bonsai tree (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Explains why Satsuki needs acidic soil and rainwater instead of hard tap water, and when to prune so you don't remove flower buds.

resources.title: Crab Apple (Malus sp.) (Phoenix Bonsai)
resources.why: Recommends removing all the fruit one year in three so a potted crabapple doesn't wear itself out, which shows the cost of fruit load clearly.

resources.title: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map
resources.why: Enter your ZIP code to get your extreme winter low, the number that decides how much your calendar has to shift from the textbook.

resources.title: Bonsai care timeline (Storm The Castle)
resources.why: A ready month-by-month timeline you can copy and then change for your own species and climate.

resources.title: Bonsai Care for Beginners: A Monthly Guide to Maintenance
resources.why: Goes through the year month by month, a quick model for filling in the rows of your own species template.

resources.title: Overwintering Bonsai trees (Bonsai Empire)
resources.why: Covers the 'protection' row of the calendar, where a mistake does the most damage.
